- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially in early/medium horizon.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast, particularly if recent price is falling.
- Overshoots after sharp upward spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3-5 days) are common; cap forecast at 10-15% above peak for next 5-7 days.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, adjust downward by 2-5% unless sentiment strongly bullish.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates true price by 2-5% in bullish sentiment periods; add 1-2% buffer if sentiment > 0.6.
- If sentiment swings sharply (e.g., +0.5 to -0.5 in 3 days), model reacts too slowly; adjust forecast 1-2 days ahead to match sentiment momentum.
- Avoid overfitting to recent 3-5 day highs; if forecast is >10% above 5-day high, reduce by 3-5% unless sentiment confirms breakout.
